key_insight: Instead of enumerating which subsets of temporal properties are realizable, the paper computes in one symbolic fixed-point pass a relation between product-game states and all realizable goal sets, and synthesizes strategies that achieve maximal realizable sets.
problem_solved: It addresses LTLf synthesis with multiple, potentially conflicting properties where satisfying them all may be impossible; prior methods required costly enumeration of subsets of properties, leading to exponential blowup and poor scalability.
method: Construct a product game over the system and all LTLf properties and introduce Boolean goal variables that represent which properties are achieved.
Perform a single monotone fixed-point computation that yields, for each product-game state, the set (implicitly represented) of goal combinations realizable from that state.
Synthesize strategies that maximize realizable goal sets using the symbolic representation to avoid explicit enumeration of exponentially many combinations.
impact: Provides a scalable, fully symbolic technique for synthesizing controllers under multiple conflicting temporal objectives, enabling practitioners to obtain optimal trade-off strategies with formal guarantees without combinatorial enumeration.
visual_elements: Illustrated product-game graph with nodes labeled by Boolean goal variables and edges for system/environment moves
Diagram of the monotone fixed-point iteration converging to a relation mapping states to realizable goal-sets (showing compression vs. naive enumeration)
Lattice or Boolean hypercube visualization showing implicit representation of exponentially many goal combinations and highlighted maximal realizable sets
Example environment overlay showing a synthesized strategy that maximizes satisfied properties (policy traced on scenario)
paper_authors: Christoph Weinhuber, Yannik Schnitzer, Alessandro Abate, David Parker, Giuseppe De Giacomo
